To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic recording is affected by the following four factors: (i) the foreign body response to implant, (ii) the mechanical stress to the implant, (iii) the electrical noise, and (iv) the degradation of the recording interface.

the chronic recording of neural probes is limited by the foreign body response, which is affected by the implantation site, probe size, material, and coating, and that the coating material, coating method, and the probe design are critical factors for minimizing the foreign body response and achieving reliable chronic recording.
the chronic reliability of a neural probe is dependent on the probe’s structural shape and material, and that the chronic recording performance is dependent on the recording site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of neural probes that are not only capable of high fidelity recording, but also reliable for chronic applications.
the development and evaluation of neural probes for chronic applications, with a particular focus on chronic reliability.
the fabrication of novel neural probes for chronic applications and the development of a chronic recording system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chronic recording performance of a neural probe is a result of the combined effect of various factors that are affected by the probe’s structural design, material selection, and fabrication method.
there is no one single solution for the chronic recording problem; rather, it is a multi-faceted problem and thus requires a multi-facetted solution.
chronic recording with neural probes is still a challenge, but the challenge is not insurmountable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic reliability of neural probes is not only determined by the structural design of the neural probes, but also by the implantation procedure, post-implantation care, and the animal species used for experiments.
neural probes that can record chronically are not yet developed.
the chronic reliability of neural probes is highly correlated with the implantation site and the probe design.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the chronic foreign body responses to implantation are inevitable, and the key to achieving chronic viability is not to eliminate the foreign body response, but to minimize its impact by designing the neural probes to be more compatible with the body.
chronic reliability of neural probes can be improved by minimizing the factors affecting chronic recording.
chronic reliability of neural probes can be improved through careful consideration of the probe geometry, materials, and surface modification methods.
